issues_detected.description: Version ordering is non-monotonic: this June 2026 release is recorded as version '2.0', while version_access states that the June 2025 and October 2025 releases were both at version 2.1, and the citation string ends 'V2'. A later release carrying a lower version string than its predecessors makes version identity ambiguous for citation and reuse.
issues_detected.recommendation: Reconcile the release version with the Dataverse version sequence (e.g. V3/2.2 for the June 2026 release) and state the Dataverse major.minor version explicitly alongside the release name.

issues_detected.description: All named software describes the MuSIC cell-map construction pipeline (node2vec, DenseNet-121, HiDeF, GPT-4 via the Gene Set AI pipeline, Cell Mapping Toolkit), but known_limitations states that this release 'does not contain predicted cell maps'. FAIRSCAPE is named only for RO-Crate packaging and provenance-metadata production. No software is named for producing or transforming the data actually distributed here, including the two processed_data collections (cm4ai_mass-spec_* SEC-MS data and cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas): no MS search/quantitation tool, no single-cell alignment or guide-calling tool, and no named tool for the quality control referenced in cleaning_strategies.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name and version the software that produced the distributed processed data (e.g. the MS search/quantitation software for the SEC-MS tables and the alignment/perturbation-calling software for the Perturb-seq cell atlas), and attach it via used_software on the relevant preprocessing_strategies and cleaning_strategies entries.

issues_detected.description: No variable-level metadata is provided anywhere (variables is absent), although the release includes tabular processed outputs (SEC-MS elution profile tables and a Perturb-seq cell atlas mapping phenotypes for 11,739 targeted genes). Reusers cannot determine column identifiers, units, or value semantics without downloading the archives.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add variables entries with identifiers, data types and descriptions for the tabular components of the SEC-MS and Perturb-seq deliverables, or reference the RO-Crate data dictionary that defines them.

issues_detected.description: Distribution formats resolve only to the container level: 'ZIP Archive' / application/zip plus RO-Crate packaging. The formats and character encodings of the files inside the archives (e.g. mzML/mzTab for MS, TIFF/PNG for confocal images, FASTQ/h5ad/MTX for Perturb-seq) are not stated, and no encoding is given for any file.
issues_detected.recommendation: Declare per-collection format, media_type and encoding for the files within each ZIP archive so that tooling can be selected before download.

issues_detected.description: No change descriptions or errata are provided for this release. updates carries a forward-looking cadence ('quarterly', through November 2026) but no statement of what changed relative to the October 2025 release, and errata is absent; the reader must infer changes from the description's content enumeration and the is_new_version_of relationships.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add per-release change notes (datasets added, embargoes lifted, files replaced) and an errata list, or record them in updates.update_details as release-specific notes.

issues_detected.description: Data anomalies and missing-data handling are not documented: anomalies and missing_data_documentation are both absent, and cleaning_strategies records only that single-cell CRISPR screen QC was in progress at preprint time, without outcomes. Sampling limitations are documented, but observed quality defects (failed antibodies, low-depth wells, dropped guides, batch effects) are not.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add anomalies entries for known per-modality quality defects and a missing_data_documentation entry describing missingness patterns (e.g. proteins imaged in only a subset of conditions) and how users should handle them.

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified states a determination and its rationale ('cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject'; 'De-identified Samples: Yes') rather than a named method, and lists no identifiers_removed. The rationale is semantically appropriate for commercially sourced, non-clinical cell-line material, but the sub-element's 'named method' expectation (Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity) is not literally satisfied.
issues_detected.recommendation: State explicitly that no de-identification transformation was applied by the producers because source material arrived de-identified from ATCC and HipSci, and cite the vendor/consortium de-identification basis.

issues_detected.description: The dedicated download_url slot is unpopulated. Access is nonetheless actionable: distribution_formats.access_urls gives the persistent UVA Dataverse dataset URL, the notes describe direct file download and the Data Access API, and every file_collections entry carries a path and MD5.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate download_url with the Dataverse persistent-identifier download endpoint so machine clients need not parse distribution notes.

issues_detected.description: Ethics contact affiliation is inconsistent across fields: creators lists Vardit Ravitsky at the University of Montreal, while ethical_reviews gives her contact email at thehastingscenter.org and the description lists the Hastings Center among collaborating institutions.
issues_detected.recommendation: Align the ethics contact's institutional affiliation with the contact address, or note the dual affiliation explicitly.

issues_detected.description: Stated update cadence is quarterly, but the recorded release history (March 2025, June 2025, October 2025, June 2026) shows an eight-month interval between the October 2025 and June 2026 releases, and immunofluorescence files in this release were published a month after the release date (2026-07-15 vs 2026-06-17).
issues_detected.recommendation: Either qualify the cadence claim (target vs achieved) or note the schedule deviation and staged file publication in release notes.

issues_detected.description: publisher is given as a bare ROR CURIE (ROR:0153tk833) with no human-readable label. The identifier resolves to the University of Virginia and agrees with the 10.18130 Dataverse DOI prefix and the citation's 'University of Virginia Dataverse', so this is a readability rather than a validity defect.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the publisher as a labelled object (name plus ROR id), and name the repository (University of Virginia Dataverse) rather than only the institution.

issues_detected.description: No imputation_protocols entry is present, not even an explicit statement that imputation was not used, despite mass-spectrometry data where missing-value handling is a standard analytical concern.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add an imputation_protocols entry stating either the imputation approach used for SEC-MS/AP-MS intensity gaps or that no imputation was applied to the distributed data.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C is well formed and its prefix is a plausible registrant (University of Virginia Dataverse), consistent with publisher ROR:0153tk833, the citation string, and version_access.latest_version_doi — four fields agreeing on the same identifier.

NIH award identifiers are internally coherent and format-valid: 1OT2OD032742-01 with core project OT2OD032742 and supplement 3OT2OD032742-01S2 (OT2 activity code, OD institute), plus 5U54HG012513-02 for the Bridge2AI Bridge Center; the award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31 brackets the release date.

The absence of human-subject, consent, privacy and compensation documentation is semantically correct rather than a gap: description and keywords identify commercially sourced cell lines (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J), direct_collection.is_direct is false with an explanatory note, and collection_mechanisms describe instruments and CRISPR screens rather than participant recruitment.

Cell-line provenance is given with Cellosaurus RRIDs (RRID:CVCL_0419, RRID:CVCL_B5P3) and named sources (ATCC, HipSci), which is the field-appropriate way to make non-human-subject biological provenance verifiable.

License semantics are consistently propagated: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, data_use_permission no_commercial_use, a prohibited_uses entry naming commercial use, and ip_restrictions identifying the UC Regents and Stanford as the copyright holders from whom a commercial licence must be negotiated.

known_biases uses a taxonomy-aligned bias_type (representation_bias) and its rationale matches sampling_strategies.is_representative=false and why_not_representative verbatim in substance — a genuine cross-field consistency, not duplicated boilerplate.

Subset structure is semantically rich and cross-checks against the modality coverage claimed in the description: seven is_subpopulation subsets spanning three MDA-MB-468 treatment conditions and four KOLF2.1J states, matching the per-condition coverage stated in subpopulations.distribution and the ten file_collections.

The record distinguishes project-level aggregate figures (1,374 interactions, 53,788 images, 21.4 TB) from release-level values and declines to assert the former as slot values, and resolves a conflicting image count (563 vs 464) by source rank — evidence of disciplined provenance reasoning rather than uncritical aggregation.

Governance is documented as an operating structure rather than a claim: a named Data Access Committee, an access_review_process covering dual licensing for commercial use, stewardship roles, and a committee contact that agrees between data_governance.committee_contact and regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact.
File-level integrity is verifiable: each of the ten collections carries a path, compression, human-readable size, publication date and MD5 checksum.

excluded_item_ids: E4.3 Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
E4.4 Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
E4.5 Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
overall_score.denominator_note: normalized_percentage = 43/47 x 100 (N/A-adjusted basis); fixed_percentage = 43/50 x 100 (whole-rubric basis). The three excluded items are Element 4 sub-elements 3-5, gated on the human-subjects condition, which fails on Element 1 and Element 8 evidence (cell-line description, instrument-based collection mechanisms). Element 4 sub-elements 1-2 remain applicable on the governance disjunct and are scored. Comparability requires matching evaluator model, instrument digest, and excluded item identities.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; cell-line RRIDs RRID:CVCL_0419 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3 in direct_collection
sub_elements.quality_note: A single persistent DOI is used consistently as the dataset id, the doi slot, the latest-version pointer and inside the citation string. Prior releases are given their own distinct DOIs, so release identity is unambiguous.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: DOI matches 10.XXXX/... ; prefix 10.18130 is a plausible registrant (University of Virginia Dataverse) and agrees with publisher ROR:0153tk833 and the citation's named repository. RRIDs follow the Cellosaurus CVCL_ pattern. Format valid and prefix plausible: score 1.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description ~1,900 characters enumerating Perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS and immunofluorescence content per cell line and treatment condition, the overarching objective, the RO-Crate/FAIRSCAPE packaging, the three pillars and six modules, and nine collaborating institutions
sub_elements.quality_note: Far beyond the 200-character threshold and specific throughout: named cell lines, named drugs, named modalities, named differentiated cell types, and a stated scientific objective. A reader can tell what is and is not in this release from the description alone.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Description content is semantically appropriate to the claimed dataset type (multi-modal in vitro functional genomics) and matches keywords, instances, subsets and file_collections; program context (Bridge2AI Functional Genomics Grand Challenge) is stated in the description and corroborated by keywords and funders.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 28 terms including AI, AP-MS, breast cancer, Bridge2AI, cardiomyocyte, CM4AI, CRISPR/Cas9, iPSC, KOLF2.1J, MDA-MB-468, paclitaxel, perturb-seq, protein-protein interaction, SEC-MS, scRNAseq, size exclusion chromatography, subcellular imaging, vorinostat
sub_elements.quality_note: Well above the five-keyword threshold and spanning four distinct axes: domain (breast cancer, AI), assay (AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, scRNAseq), biological material (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J, NPC, neuron, cardiomyocyte) and perturbagen (paclitaxel, vorinostat). Synonym pairs (AP-MS / affinity purification; NPC / neural progenitor cell) aid retrieval.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Every keyword is corroborated elsewhere in the record; no keyword stuffing with unsupported terms. 'mass spectroscopy' is a loose usage for mass spectrometry but the correct term is used in acquisition_methods.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/; distribution_formats.access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; file_collections lists ten named collections with paths, compression, sizes, dates and MD5s; total_file_count: 10
sub_elements.quality_note: Two complementary entry points are given (project release page and the repository landing page), and the ten-collection file structure substitutes for a nested resources list with more detail than a bare hierarchy would carry.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Both URLs are structurally valid with plausible domains; the Dataverse URL embeds the same persistent identifier recorded in doi and id. The dedicated resources slot is empty, but the hierarchical content requirement is satisfied by file_collections and subsets.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: four is_new_version_of links to the October 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM), June 2025 (F3TD5R), March 2025 (B35XWX) and May 2024 (DXWOS5) releases; is_described_by doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311; is_referenced_by doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734; subsets: seven identified subsets with #fragment identifiers under the dataset DOI
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationships are typed, targeted by resolvable DOI, and named. The seven subsets use DOI-fragment identifiers derived from the parent DOI, giving an explicit internal hierarchy. source_caveats explains the editorial decision not to merge earlier releases into this record.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship types are used correctly (superseding releases as is_new_version_of, preprints as is_described_by / is_referenced_by). parent_datasets is empty, which is semantically correct for a top-level release; the lineage is expressed through versioning relationships instead.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 statement with the four obligations (credit, license link, indication of changes, ShareAlike) and the non-commercial limit; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; contact_person: Trey Ideker; ip_restrictions.restrictions: 'Copyright is held by the Regents of the University of California except where otherwise noted; spatial proteomics raw image data is copyright the Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University. Commercial use requires a separate license negotiation with the copyright holder (UCSD, Stanford, and/or UCSF depending upon the specific data package in question).'
sub_elements.quality_note: Actionable rather than nominal: the licence obligations are enumerated, the commercial pathway is named, and the IP statement identifies which institution holds rights over which data package and whom to approach.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: License, data_use_permission enum, prohibited_uses and ip_restrictions all agree on the non-commercial restriction and on the same rights holders; no contradiction between openness claims and restriction claims.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions: 'The release records FDA Regulated: No'; regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant: not_applicable; regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact: Jillian Parker (ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486); data_governance.committee_name: CM4AI Data Access Committee with committee_contact and access_review_process; confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present false with details 'The release records Human Subjects: No; De-identified Samples: Yes; FDA Regulated: No.'
sub_elements.quality_note: The regulatory posture is stated explicitly with its basis rather than left blank, and the responsible governance contact required by this sub-element's full scope is named twice with an ORCID and an email. The confidentiality classification is carried by confidential_elements and sensitive_elements as reasoned false flags rather than as an enum value.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: HIPAA not_applicable is semantically correct for non-clinical cell-line data and is consistent with human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=false. The confidentiality_level enum is unpopulated and no export-control or GDPR/CCPA assessment is recorded, which is a scope gap rather than an error; the governance-contact and compliance-status components are present and substantive, so the item passes.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats.access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C with notes 'Individual files below the download size limit may be downloaded directly; the Data Access API is available for programmatic access'; file_collections give ten resolvable paths with MD5 checksums; page: https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/
sub_elements.quality_note: Platform access instructions are concrete: the repository landing URL, the direct-download size caveat, and the programmatic API route. Combined with per-file paths and checksums a user can both retrieve and verify the data.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The dedicated download_url slot is empty (flagged as a low-severity completeness issue), but the sub-element's purpose - a retrievable link or platform access instructions - is met by evidence in distribution_formats and file_collections. Scored on documented retrievability, not on slot placement.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: [{format: ZIP Archive, media_type: application/zip, access_urls: [...]}, {format: RO-Crate, notes: 'packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework'}]; file_collections each declare compression: zip and a collection_type (raw_data / processed_data / metadata); raw_data_sources.raw_data_format: 'Confocal microscopy image with four color channels'
sub_elements.quality_note: Both a concrete container format with a correct MIME type and a recognised packaging standard are declared, and each collection is typed by role. Enough for a user to know what will arrive and that it is self-describing.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: media_type application/zip correctly matches format 'ZIP Archive'. The formats of the files inside the archives and their encodings are not declared, recorded as a medium-severity completeness issue; the item passes on the container and RO-Crate declarations.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: six typed links with DOIs; external_resources: eleven entries including MassIVE depositions for iPSC and cancer-cell SEC-MS and for both AP-MS conditions, SRA via NCBI BioProject, Figshare CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas, the cm4ai.org portal, https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, https://fairscape.github.io (MIT licence), http://integrativemodeling.org; one entry carries restrictions: 'Embargoed at the time of the June 2026 release'
sub_elements.quality_note: Unusually thorough: raw-data repositories, code, documentation and modelling software are all linked, with archival flags distinguishing preservation repositories from project resources, and the embargoed component is disclosed rather than omitted.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Repository choices are domain-appropriate (MassIVE for MS, SRA for sequencing, Figshare for the atlas) and consistent with third_party_sharing.is_shared=true and with the embargo recorded in known_limitations. Accession numbers are not given for the external depositions, which weakens but does not defeat the link.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on non-E3 evidence: distribution_formats populated with access_urls to the UVA Dataverse record, ten file_collections with paths and checksums, page: https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/, and license CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 explicitly permitting sharing and adaptation.
sub_elements.evidence: license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Users are free to share and adapt the material, provided appropriate credit is given, a link to the license is provided, changes are indicated, the material is not used for commercial purposes, and contributions are distributed under the same license.'
sub_elements.quality_note: A named, standard, machine-recognisable licence with its reuse permissions and obligations spelled out, plus a named contact and a stated route to commercial licensing. A reuser can determine permissibility without further enquiry.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 is used correctly and consistently with data_use_permission: no_commercial_use, the prohibited_uses commercial-use entry, and ip_restrictions; the NC and SA terms are restrictive but reuse for research is unambiguously allowed.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met as above (distribution_formats, file_collections, Dataverse access_urls, reuse-permitting licence).
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats.format: ZIP Archive with media_type application/zip; distribution_formats.format: RO-Crate; conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; file_collections.compression: zip for all ten collections; raw_data_sources.raw_data_format: 'Confocal microscopy image with four color channels'
sub_elements.quality_note: Standardisation is claimed at the packaging level with a recognised community standard (RO-Crate, with provenance graphs) and a correct MIME type, which is genuinely actionable for tooling. It stops short of the payload: the formats and character encodings of the archive contents are not declared.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: RO-Crate is a legitimate standardised packaging format and the claim is corroborated by conforms_to and conforms_to_standard. Encoding is absent for every file and payload formats (mzML, TIFF, FASTQ, h5ad) are unstated - recorded as a medium-severity issue. Passes on the standard-format declaration; the gap is noted rather than ignored.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met as above.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances use ontology CURIEs B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:63, B2AI_TOPIC:12, B2AI_TOPIC:15, B2AI_TOPIC:26; labeling_strategies align maps to Gene Ontology and Reactome
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is stated at three levels - packaging standard, metadata schema with a resolvable w3id URI and class, and controlled vocabulary use for substrates and topics - plus named reference ontologies for annotation. This is what interoperability documentation should look like.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The w3id schema URI is structurally valid and the declared class (Dataset) matches the record's shape; CURIE prefixes are used consistently. GO and Reactome are correctly characterised as protein function and pathway resources.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on non-E3 evidence (distribution_formats, file_collections, Dataverse access_urls, reuse-permitting licence), so this item is scored rather than excluded; its own emptiness is not a ground for exclusion under the anti-circular rule.
sub_elements.evidence: variables: absent from the record. No data dictionary, column list, unit declaration or value-set definition appears anywhere; instances.notes describe image channels and gene counts in prose only.
sub_elements.quality_note: Fails: there is no variable-level metadata at all, despite the release containing tabular processed outputs (SEC-MS elution profiles and a Perturb-seq cell atlas over 11,739 targeted genes) whose columns and identifiers would need defining for integration with other datasets.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: is_tabular: false partially explains the absence for the image and raw-sequence archives, but two of the ten collections are typed processed_data and would carry variables. The prose in instances.notes is not a substitute for identified variables.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: five categories with usage_notes (AI-ready research data, AI model training, cellular process analysis, perturbation and disease-context analysis, bioinformatics analysis of component datasets - the last noting the release 'is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the individual datasets, as computed cell maps are not included'); prohibited_uses: clinical decision-making or patient care without regulatory oversight, and commercial use under CC BY-NC-SA; discouraged_uses: use without domain expertise, use as a complete cell-map resource at this stage
sub_elements.quality_note: All three guidance categories are populated with reasons, and the guidance is calibrated to this specific release rather than generic - it steers users away from expecting cell maps and warns that domain expertise is required.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Prohibited uses are consistent with the licence (commercial) and with the non-clinical nature of the data (clinical decision-making); discouraged uses are consistent with known_limitations on interim scope. No contradiction between intended and prohibited use statements.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition fails on external evidence (E1 description names commercially sourced cell lines MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J; keywords carry no participant, patient or clinical-research terms; E8 collection_mechanisms describe SEC-MS, AP-MS, confocal imaging and CRISPRi screens rather than recruitment). The governance disjunct is satisfied on E2 evidence: regulatory_restrictions names a governance_committee_contact (Jillian Parker, ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486) and data_governance declares a CM4AI Data Access Committee with an access_review_process supervising distribution and dual licensing - an applying governance structure over donor-derived material, not a record that no restriction applies. Under the ambiguity rule this resolves to applicable.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews (two entries): 'Ethical review for the CM4AI project is led by the Ethics Module, which developed a plan for ethical preparation, licensing, dissemination, and Data Access supervision of CM4AI datasets, balancing openness of the data produced with protection of intellectual property and supervision and monitoring of potential efforts at commercialization', contact_person Vardit Ravitsky (ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801, ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org), plus a second review contact Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon (Simon Fraser University, jean-christophe_belisle-pipon@sfu.ca); human_subject_research.notes records ethical sourcing of both cell lines (ATCC; HipSci via a simple MTA for not-for-profits); data_governance.access_review_process and stewardship_roles
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethics oversight is documented as a functioning structure with named, contactable reviewers, a stated remit and a described relationship to the licensing and access regime - not a boilerplate assertion of approval. Cell-line sourcing ethics (the relevant oversight question for this data type) is addressed explicitly.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistent with involves_human_subjects=false: no IRB protocol number is claimed, and none is expected. data_protection_impacts is absent, which is defensible for non-clinical cell-line data and consistent with the absent reidentification_risk assessment; no inconsistency arises because no DPIA-triggering claim is made.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same determination as sub-element 1: human-subjects condition fails on E1/E8 evidence, governance disjunct satisfied on E2 evidence (regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact; data_governance Data Access Committee with access review over distribution of donor-derived cell-line material).
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'The release records De-identified Samples: Yes. CM4AI data are distinctive within Bridge2AI in that they are non-clinical (from tissue cultures) and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.'; direct_collection.collection_details names the de-identified source lines with RRIDs and vendors; sampling_strategies.source_data describes donor characteristics at the level of tumour origin and donor demographics only
sub_elements.quality_note: The determination is stated with its reasoning and its basis in the release record, and is coherent with the data type: the material arrived de-identified from ATCC and HipSci, so the answer to how privacy risk was removed is answered at the sourcing level. Actionable for a reuser assessing privacy obligations.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: No formal method is named (no Safe Harbor, Expert Determination or k-anonymity) and no identifiers_removed list is given - recorded as a low-severity semantic_understanding issue. The claim is nonetheless semantically appropriate for in vitro cell-line data and consistent with confidential_elements_present=false and sensitive_elements_present=false; the hedge 'with current knowledge' is an accurate characterisation of residual genomic re-identification risk rather than an overclaim.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Participant condition fails on evidence external to Element 4: E1 description and keywords reference only commercially sourced cell lines and their derivatives (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J iPSCs, NPCs, neurons, cardiomyocytes) with no participant, patient or clinical-research terms, and E8 collection_mechanisms describe instruments and CRISPRi screens rather than human participant recruitment. There are no participants whose privacy could be protected. Per #1060 the governance disjunct does not reach sub-elements 3-5: the CM4AI Data Access Committee and the pre-publication embargo are governance structures, not a participant signal.
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk are absent; the record instead documents at the material level that data 'cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject' (sensitive_elements, is_deidentified).
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator (-1). Scoring 0 here would measure the dataset's subject matter - in vitro cell lines rather than people - instead of its documentation quality.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Participant condition fails on the same external evidence: E1 description names cell lines, not participants; E8 collection_mechanisms and data_collectors describe laboratory generation at UCSF, Stanford and UCSD; direct_collection.is_direct is false. The governance disjunct does not extend to this sub-element (#1060).

sub_elements.quality_note: The negative determinations are explicit and reasoned rather than left blank, which is meaningful documentation: a reuser learns the basis on which no sensitivity or content warning applies, and the three flags corroborate one another.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Explicit false flags are treated as documentation, not absence, per the instrument. The determinations are semantically appropriate to in vitro cell-line data and consistent with is_deidentified and human_subject_research. content_warnings carries the flag without detail, but sensitive_elements supplies the reasoning.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries - the Ethics Module-led review with its remit ('a plan for ethical preparation, licensing, dissemination, and Data Access supervision of CM4AI datasets, balancing openness of the data produced with protection of intellectual property and supervision and monitoring of potential efforts at commercialization') and two named, contactable reviewers with ORCIDs and emails. future_use_impacts: 'Anticipating potential applications of the data and derived AI/ML systems, integrating them into data governance frameworks to optimize benefits and mitigate potential risks, and promoting their use for the collective good, is a stated ethical requirement of the project'; and an Ethics team toolset 'aimed at enhancing awareness and comprehension of the ethical, legal, and social ramifications associated with CM4AI data and the consequent AI systems'. data_governance records the Ethics team's collaboration with the Data Acquisition, Tools and Standards modules.
sub_elements.quality_note: Both halves of the sub-element are met: a described ethics review structure with named reviewers, and a forward-looking social impact analysis that addresses the consequences of AI systems derived from the data rather than only the data themselves.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Social impact reasoning is appropriately scoped to a non-human-subject resource whose risks are downstream and dual-use rather than privacy-based, and is consistent with the Data Access Committee's commercialisation-monitoring remit. Conflicts of interest are not addressed; impacts are stated as programme commitments rather than as a completed assessment with identified risks.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on non-E10 evidence: distribution_formats populated with Dataverse access_urls, ten file_collections with paths, sizes and MD5s, and a reuse-permitting CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence.
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: ROR:0153tk833; distribution_formats.access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; citation names 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; retention_limit: 'Long term preservation in the University of Virginia Dataverse, supported by committed institutional funds'; component raw data additionally deposited in MassIVE, SRA and Figshare per external_resources
sub_elements.quality_note: The hosting platform is an established institutional Dataverse with a stated long-term preservation commitment, and domain repositories carry the raw components - a two-tier publication strategy appropriate to the data types.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: publisher is a bare ROR CURIE without a label, recorded as a low-severity readability issue; the identifier resolves to the University of Virginia and agrees with the 10.18130 DOI prefix and the citation, so platform identity is verifiable. Note the publisher slot names the institution rather than the repository.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Scored whenever the datasets-shared condition is met, per #1080; an existing publication is not required for applicability. Shared condition met as above.
sub_elements.evidence: citation: full recommended citation listing all authors, year 2026, title 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)', https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; related_datasets links the describing preprint doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 and a referencing preprint doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734
sub_elements.quality_note: A ready-to-use citation string in repository house style, with a resolvable DOI URL and a version designator, plus DOIs for the methods publications a citing author would also want. Nothing further is needed to credit the dataset.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The DOI in the citation matches doi, id and version_access.latest_version_doi. The citation's 'V2' does not match version '2.0' and sits oddly against the 2.1 recorded for two earlier releases - part of the medium-severity version-consistency issue. Preprint DOIs use the valid 10.1101 bioRxiv prefix.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met as above.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; description: 'packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework'; cm4ai_release_metadata.zip ships the RO-Crate metadata and provenance graphs; community identifier systems used throughout - ORCID for people, ROR for institutions, RRID/Cellosaurus for cell lines, B2AI_TOPIC/B2AI_SUBSTRATE CURIEs, DOIs for datasets and publications
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is not merely asserted: the standardised metadata is shipped as a release artefact, and community identifier systems are used consistently across people, organisations, materials and datasets. This is strong ecosystem integration.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: RO-Crate and the Bridge2AI data-sheets schema are named correctly and the declared class matches the record's structure; identifier prefixes are used in their proper namespaces. No clinical-interoperability standards (OMOP, FHIR) are claimed, which is semantically correct for non-clinical proteomic and imaging data.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met as above.
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/; external_resources: 'CM4AI project web portal at https://cm4ai.org, providing documentation, data releases, tools, publications, and training materials', the Cell Mapping Toolkit with documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, FAIRSCAPE 'described with a tutorial and installation instructions at https://fairscape.github.io'; existing_uses: a March 2024 virtual CodeFest with 38 registrants 'accompanied by detailed tutorials explaining how the data were derived and integrated and providing production-ready software for producing the datasets'; other_tasks describes asynchronous virtual training and an in-person internship co-hosted at Yale and UCSD; maintainers lists a programme-manager and website-support contact
sub_elements.quality_note: Outreach is documented as delivered activity with attendance figures and curriculum content, not just as links: tutorials, a code fest, an internship programme, and installation-level software documentation.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All URLs are structurally valid with plausible domains; the training claims are consistent with the workforce-development gap stated in addressing_gaps and with the Skills and Workforce Development module named in the description.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met as above.
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM (October 2025), doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R (June 2025), doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX (March 2025), doi:10.18130/V3/DXWOS5 (May 2024, with a note citing the preprint's Data and Software Availability Statement); is_described_by doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311; is_referenced_by doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734
sub_elements.quality_note: Six relationships, each with an explicit type, a resolvable DOI target and a human-readable name - enough for a machine agent to reconstruct the release lineage and find the describing literature.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship types are semantically correct and non-redundant: superseded releases as is_new_version_of, the methods preprint as is_described_by, and the perturbation atlas preprint as is_referenced_by. Targets use valid Dataverse and bioRxiv DOI prefixes.

strengths: Exceptional identifier discipline: one persistent DOI used consistently across id, doi, citation and latest_version_doi, with ORCIDs for 40+ creators, ROR for institutions, Cellosaurus RRIDs for both cell lines, and DOIs for every superseded release and describing preprint.

Applicability reasoning is done correctly by the record itself: human_subject_research=false, direct_collection.is_direct=false and reasoned false flags for confidential, sensitive and identifiable elements are stated with their basis, so a reader can tell that the absent consent and privacy documentation reflects in vitro cell-line data rather than an omission.

Provenance is documented in both directions - upstream to the generating laboratories (Krogan, Lundberg, UCSD) and to archival depositions in MassIVE, SRA and Figshare, and downstream through RO-Crate provenance graphs shipped as a release artefact with per-file MD5 checksums.

Funding transparency is complete and verifiable: two NIH awards with format-valid numbers, core project and supplement forms, administering organisation, project period and FY award amount, plus a named non-federal institutional fund.

Limitations are disclosed against the project's own interest - the release does not contain the predicted cell maps that are its headline product, modality protein sets overlap incompletely, and part of the content is embargoed - with mitigation stated where one exists.

Source-conflict handling is exemplary: divergent image counts (563 vs 464) and a conflicting author affiliation are surfaced in source_caveats with the resolution rule stated, and project-level aggregates are explicitly withheld from release-level slots.
weaknesses: No software is named for producing or transforming the data actually distributed: the documented tooling (node2vec, DenseNet-121, HiDeF, GPT-4/GSAI, Cell Mapping Toolkit, MuSIC) builds cell maps the release explicitly excludes, while FAIRSCAPE only packaged the release, leaving the provenance of the two processed_data collections unstated.

Variable-level metadata is entirely absent, so the tabular deliverables (SEC-MS elution profiles, the Perturb-seq cell atlas over 11,739 genes) cannot be integrated with other datasets without downloading and reverse-engineering them.

Data quality documentation stops at sampling design: anomalies and missing_data_documentation are empty, and the only cleaning statement reports that QC was in progress at preprint time without stating what it found.

No change log or errata: a reader cannot determine what was added, replaced, corrected or unembargoed relative to the October 2025 release, and the version string '2.0' is lower than the 2.1 recorded for two earlier releases.

Format declarations resolve only to the ZIP container and RO-Crate packaging; payload formats and character encodings inside the archives are never stated, and no imputation_protocols entry exists even to record that imputation was not used.
External depositions are named by repository (MassIVE, SRA, Figshare) but without accession numbers, so the archival links are not directly resolvable.
recommendations: Attach used_software, with versions and repository or software DOIs, to the preprocessing_strategies and cleaning_strategies entries that generated the released SEC-MS tables and the Perturb-seq cell atlas, naming the MS search/quantitation tool and the read-alignment and guide-calling tools; keep the cell-map pipeline tooling but mark clearly that its outputs are not in this release.
Add variables entries with identifiers, types, units and descriptions for the tabular components, and declare per-collection format, media_type and encoding for the files inside each ZIP archive.

Populate anomalies with observed per-modality quality defects (failed antibodies, low-depth or dropped guides, batch effects) and add missing_data_documentation describing missingness patterns and recommended handling; record the outcome of the CRISPR screen QC rather than its status.

Add release-specific change notes and an errata list, and reconcile the version identifier with the Dataverse version sequence so that '2.0' does not follow two 2.1 releases; align the citation's version designator with the version slot.

Record accession numbers for the MassIVE, SRA/BioProject and Figshare depositions, populate download_url with the Dataverse download endpoint, and give publisher a human-readable label naming the University of Virginia Dataverse alongside ROR:0153tk833.

Complete the regulatory scope by setting confidentiality_level and adding an imputation_protocols entry (even to state that no imputation was applied), and align the ethics contact's affiliation with her contact address.
